questions.q: If a child component dispatches a custom event named `caseselect`, how does its parent listen for it in the parent's template?
options: <c-case-row onCaseSelect={handleCaseSelect}></c-case-row>
<c-case-row listen-caseselect={handleCaseSelect}></c-case-row>
<c-case-row event="caseselect" handler={handleCaseSelect}></c-case-row>
<c-case-row oncaseselect={handleCaseSelect}></c-case-row>
questions.explain: The listener attribute is the event name prefixed with `on`, all lowercase: `oncaseselect`, written directly on the child's tag -- matching the same case-insensitive naming rule custom events must follow.

questions.q: In the parent's handler `handleCaseSelect(event)`, how does it read the payload the child attached when dispatching the event?
options: event.payload.caseId
event.data.caseId
event.detail.caseId
this.detail.caseId
questions.explain: The parent's handler receives the same event object the child dispatched, with the same `detail` payload -- nothing is transformed or renamed in between, so it reads `event.detail.caseId`.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say the dispatch-then-listen pattern keeps a child component more reusable?
options: Because the child only describes what happened and has no idea who's listening or what they'll do about it, so the same child can be dropped into different parents that each react differently
Because the child decides what happens after the event fires, which only works for one specific parent
Because dispatch-then-listen is required by the LWC compiler for all child components
Because events are faster to execute than calling a method directly
questions.explain: The child's responsibility ends at describing that something happened; deciding what to do about it is entirely up to whichever parent is listening. That separation lets the exact same child be reused across different parents with different reactions.

questions.q: Why can't a grandchild's plain, non-bubbling CustomEvent automatically reach a grandparent two levels up?
options: Because CustomEvents can only have one listener in the entire application
Because grandparents cannot contain more than one level of nested children in LWC

Because a plain CustomEvent only reaches a listener attached directly to the element that dispatched it -- the middle component would need to explicitly re-dispatch its own event after catching the grandchild's
Because events are deprecated for any communication beyond one level
questions.explain: Without bubbling/composed options set, an event is only visible to a listener on the exact element that dispatched it. Reaching a grandparent requires the intermediate component to explicitly catch the grandchild's event and re-dispatch its own.

questions.q: If `caseRow`'s event were renamed from `caseselect` to `rowselected`, what would have to change in the parent `caseList`?
options: Nothing -- the parent's listener attribute updates automatically
The parent's component class would need a new @api property
The parent's listener attribute in its template would need to change from `oncaseselect` to `onrowselected`, and the handler method name could stay whatever the developer prefers
The event's detail payload would automatically rename itself to match
questions.explain: The listener attribute is tied directly to the event's name (on + the event name), so renaming the event requires updating the parent's template listener attribute to match. The handler method's own name is unrelated and doesn't need to match the event name.
